il-prostitution-j-vacate-set.note: Fifteen of fifteen. SOURCE_IDENTITY was measured rather than deferred: this family binds zero source binaries by design and four records say so consistently, the corpus was mounted, and the receipt's allSourcesExact is true and calls itself vacuous. The fee section passes A1's ordering because the repository's Illinois fee data describes the per-Request expungement filing and is flagged county-variable throughout, while this route is Illinois's one custom_pleading track for which the legal-design record says no statewide form exists; the packet names the circuit clerk of the county of conviction and names the waiver instrument by rule number (Supreme Court Rule 298). Service is handled the way the standard asks: the State's Attorney and the 60-day objection window are stated because the repository holds them, and the one point the receipt records as unresolved — clerk service versus movant service — is sent to a named office rather than guessed.

ms-nonadj-set.note: Fifteen of fifteen, and the best fee handling of the five. The repository does hold a Mississippi figure — § 99-19-72 sets a $150 fee for each petition to expunge under § 99-19-71 — and the packet neither copies it across nor pretends not to have seen it: it states that the § 99-19-72 fee applies by its terms to § 99-19-71 petitions and does not reach § 99-15-26, which is the statute this petition pleads alone, and only then names the court office to ask and the pauper's-affidavit route. That is A1's ordering applied correctly and openly. The filing destination is stated on the petition's own face — 'petitions this court, the court that ordered nonadjudication' — matching the route census exactly.

failures.FEE_AND_WAIVER: The packet states that no held source establishes what it costs to file a CPL 160.59 sealing application, and names the clerk's office of the court of conviction to ask. The compiled New York profile answers it directly: feeRules[2] 'CPL 160.59 sealing application — No separate filing fee — Court motion; notarization needed', repeated in the profile's narrative and its agent guidance. Under A1 the stand-in is unavailable. The packet shows it can do this correctly in the same section, stating the certificate-of-disposition fee at $5 outside New York City and $10 in the five boroughs — figures the profile also holds.
failures.REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING: A systematic off-by-one in the field labels on the certificate-of-disposition request, which flows verbatim into the participant's required-facts list. Descending a vertical stack of identifier fields on page 2: ArrestNumber is labelled 'IDV Number', OrderofProtectionNumber is labelled 'Arrest Number', CertificateofDispositionNumber is labelled 'Order of Protection Number', CJTN is labelled 'Certificate of Disposition Number', NYSIDNumber is labelled 'Ticket Number', PartialDocketNumber is labelled 'NYSID Number', and ArrestDate is labelled 'Incident Date' — nine mislabelled fields, while labelBasis still claims printed_to_the_left_in_the_same_cell. Two anchors are correct and each is followed by a run of shifted labels. The participant is told to write their IDV number into the field named ArrestNumber, on the form used to obtain the certificate of disposition every 160.59 application requires.
failures.CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP: A build-introduced clipped write in pro-se-packet-boundary.pdf. Three participant values are drawn outside their own widget boxes and past the right edge of the 612-point page: Email runs to x=617.21 against a widget right edge of 572.312 — 44.89 points past the widget and 5.21 past the page — with City State Zip at 42.30/2.61 and Applicant Name at 41.68/1.99, on pages 9 and 11. Contrast the Arkansas family, whose boundary fixture refuses three over-long values rather than drawing them past the rule.
failures.SELF_HELP_STOP: Absent. This is the only one of the five families read here whose participant document contains no self-help boundary: no 'not legal advice', no referral to a lawyer or legal aid, no 'when to stop' section, no statement that the packet does not decide whether the conviction can be sealed. forTheCaptain.issue: A cross-cutting pattern, not three separate family defects: three of five packets assert that the repository holds no fee answer for their route, and in all three the compiled state profile answers it directly.
forTheCaptain.detail: Each packet's claim about its own bound source forms is correct and was confirmed here from the source bytes. Each packet's claim about the repository is false. The answers sit in src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/<STATE>.json under packetGenerator.feeRules — 'Sealing petition filing fee $0' for Arkansas, 'DOJ-CIB fingerprint arrest removal — Wisconsin DOJ says no fee is required' for Wisconsin, 'CPL 160.59 sealing application — No separate filing fee' for New York — and the national route census names that profile as a requiredSourceId for each of those exact routes.
forTheCaptain.likelyCause: The repair lanes that wrote these fee sections appear to have searched the family's own bound source PDFs and stopped there. Amendment A1's test asks a wider question: whether the repository establishes the answer.
forTheCaptain.whyItMatters: Under A1 the named-checkable-authority stand-in is only available where no held source establishes the answer, so each of these is a failure rather than a near-miss. It is also a participant harm in at least the Arkansas case, where a sworn paragraph is involved and the participant is sent to resolve a fee the profile says was abolished in 2019.
forTheCaptain.captainDecision: Whether to re-scope the fee-repair instruction across every lane so it searches the compiled state profile and the route census before writing a 'no held source establishes this' sentence. Two of my five packets already do it correctly — ms-nonadj-set engages the held $150 and gives the statutory reason it does not reach its route, and il-prostitution-j-vacate-set correctly treats county-variable range data as not establishing its route's fee — so the standard is reachable and is being met where lanes look in the right place.
